text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG declined to comment on the possibility that the Malaysian government could cancel the $5.5 billion contract over the Bakun hydroelectric dam.

An ABB spokesman repeated the company's policy of not commenting on ongoing discussions with its customers, but confirmed that another meeting with Bakun's main developer, Ekran Bhd, was scheduled within the next few weeks.
"We don't want to comment on discussions with a customer," an ABB spokesman said from the group's headquarters here.
In Kuala Lumpur, an ABB spokesman said ABB and Ekran would meet next week.
"These are ongoing discussions with a customer and that is to be expected on such a big project," the spokesman added.

Last week Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the government may intervene to resolve a dispute between ABB and Ekran and there was a remote possibility that the contract would be cancelled if the terms were found to be unfair.
The Bakun contract is the largest ever awarded to ABB and the value of the contract to ABB exceeds $2.5 billion.
The total value of the Bakun project is $6.18 billion with the value of the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) amounting to $5.5 billion.

ABB and joint contractor Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos e Obras (CBPO) are waiting for preparatory work at the dam site, such as water diversion, to be completed before they can start work on their part of the project.
Last month Malaysia's acting prime minister Anwar Ibrahim said there was a major dispute between Ekran, the main developer of the Bakun dam, and ABB over the terms of the agreement.

A rights issue by Ekran in June was heavily undersubcribed due to the bearish stock market and concerns about Bakun. It left Ekran's executive chairman, Ting Pek Khiing, taking up 150.98 million of the 161.42 million unsubscribed shares.

A third of the proceeds from the Ekran rights issue had been earmarked for financing Ekran's 32 percent stake in the Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd (BHEC), the project's operator, whose floatation has been delayed.
